every_map_contract.verbatim: - Every map contains the requested major terrain families: hills, valleys/basins, mountain ranges, plateaus, canyons/gorges, cliffs, terraces, rock pillars, dunes/dry channels, rivers/tributaries, lakes, waterfall/receiving pool and wetlands, with readable coastal terrain. These are physical terrain/water/vegetation requirements, not feature labels or random optional spawns.

- At least **eight substantial ecological regions** appear on each map: meadow/grassland, mixed woodland, cool conifer forest, montane/alpine, freshwater wetland/riparian, dry scrub/woodland, arid/badlands and warm coastal/woodland. Small maps compress geographic scale deliberately; avoid abrupt random checkerboards. Tiny islands do not each repeat the whole world catalogue.

- Biome regions have measurable area, vegetation composition/density, ground material, soil/moisture, available resources, seasonal behavior and route/settlement consequences. A recolored patch does not count as a biome. Require meaningful area and usable transitions; tiny token stamps do not satisfy the minimum.

- Keep ordinary flats and gentle slopes for living/farming among pronounced relief. The player's safe opening has above-average measured scenic quality, reachable freshwater and useful subsistence resources. Hills are distributed beyond one distant showcase; exploration reveals multiple distinct regions.

- Required families vary in arrangement, extent, shape and grandeur across seeds. Rarity controls exceptional scale and composition, not whether a required family exists. Generation may retry/repair before accepting a seed; it may not silently omit a family.

qa_additions.original_line: - Calibrate farming by cropped area, crop-specific seed and net yield, person-hours by operation, soil depth and texture, moisture and flood exposure, and edible output after processing and storage losses. A default 8.2 × 8.2 m field is 67.24 m², about 0.0166 modern acres. On the Winchester sample's 385 kg/ha net wheat benchmark that area yields about 2.6 kg before post-harvest losses. At 3,320 kcal/kg and an illustrative 2,300 kcal/day, one cropped acre provides about 225 person-days of wheat energy, with no allowance for spoilage, fallow or a varied diet. Walter of Henley gives a benchmark of 2.5 person-days per acre to reap and bind, separate from land preparation, sowing, weeding, threshing and hauling. Retain a declared simulation scale for game units rather than interpreting 260 abstract yield units as kilograms. References: [Winchester manorial yield study](https://www.bahs.org.uk/AGHR/VOLUMES/AGHR38.pdf), [Walter of Henley](https://medieval.ucdavis.edu/120D/Walter.html), [FAO grain energy conversion](https://www.fao.org/4/y9422e/y9422e04.htm), [NIST area conversion](https://pages.nist.gov/fipy/en/4.0/generated/fipy.tools.dimensions.physicalField.html).
